Draft board: two directions

DG05-CONCEPT-A, the first style-selection package for the MaddenTool class board with integrated player inspection. This is a design concept. It is not the app, and it does not show a working generator or export. Player names, draft selections, colleges, source positions and the Bob Brown correction come from a local mt-data import of the legacy lookup (as-of 2026-09-15). wAV, evidence states and career numbers are ◇ sample inputs, not any player's record, and ratings (OVR, dev tier, archetype, percentile) are illustrative layout values computed from those samples, because the ratings model (DG04b) is not built yet.

Generated or assembled. Higgsfield produced the two raw directions (purple tag). Every usable frame (blue tag) is a static HTML layout I built from those directions, with real identity data, labelled sample statistics and the original dev-trait icons inlined byte for byte, then screenshot in headless Chrome at the exact frame size. The model is not trusted to reproduce table copy or icons.
Selected by the user: A, Scouting Desk, a table with a docked player inspector. Both light and dark themes are wanted. B stays documented as the explored alternative and a source of ideas (its ledger palette for A's light theme, round bands as a possible “Group by round” view). Other generator preferences remain open.

Why A fits: with the inspector open, A keeps 33 readable rows at 1440×900, against 28 for B. Its docked inspector can grow into the full DG05b profile editor (seven rating groups, persona DNA, undo history), which B's 150px inline band cannot hold. And A reaches 800×600 by dropping columns rather than re-arranging. B's real strength is that the generator recipe and provenance are always visible. A keeps the same facts on one chip line and in the status bar, one click away.

A · Scouting Desk (dark) — selected

  • Hierarchy: player first. Table, then a docked 392px inspector; settings as chips; counts in the status bar.
  • Gains: the most rows; the inspector scales to editing; keyboard flow is row to inspector; the same structure works at 800×600.
  • Costs: changing the lens or hindsight takes a popover from a chip; the generator recipe is less prominent; the inspector costs width.

B · Class Ledger (light) — explored alternative

  • Hierarchy: class first. A permanent recipe column, round-banded table and inline inspection.
  • Gains: lens, hindsight, seed, spoilers and data provenance are always in view; the round bands match how people think about drafts; the row and its details stay together.
  • Costs: the inline band drops the view to 28 rows and is too short for editing; the 262px recipe column is always taken, even while reviewing; at 800×600 the recipe must collapse anyway.

Raw Higgsfield outputs

Shown for provenance and mood only. Both were generated from the prompts in source/higgsfield-prompts.json with gpt_image_2_5 (flare, quality high, 2k, 27:16 → 2592×1536), then resized to 1440 wide with a caption strip. Nothing in them is repainted.

Still open (not settled by these frames)

The board direction is settled (A, selected by the user). Still open: default lens, Career cap, export size (389 or 402), whether the seed shows by default, single window or several, and the final name. The frames use example settings and label them “example”. Full record: DECISIONS.md beside this file.
